context: Goro-grandpa drives Sho-young in his old truck; talks of younger days.
purpose: Elder driving and reminiscing with child.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.en: Grandpa, your car is really old!
lines.style: Bright, unfiltered observation without judgment. Quick, wondering tone. Leans forward slightly with genuine curiosity. No meanness — just stating what he notices.

lines.speaker: goro_grandpa
lines.jp: うん、若い頃から乗っとる。
lines.en: Yeah, I've been driving it since I was young.
lines.style: Quiet, patient smile in the voice. No defensiveness. A gentle acceptance of the car's age, even affection for it. Unhurried pace, like he's looking out the window.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.style: Quick, eager bounce. Eyes bright with anticipation. The question of a child who trusts the answer will be interesting. No doubt, just excitement about the next thing.

lines.speaker: goro_grandpa
lines.en: A road I used to drive a lot, back in the day.
lines.style: Soft, reflective pause before speaking. Voice carries the weight of memory without sadness. Slow pace, like he's watching the road appear in his mind. Steady hands on the wheel.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.style: Hopeful lilt at the end. Seeking confirmation, sensing the nostalgia in Grandpa's tone and wanting it to match his own energy. Warm, trusting the answer will be yes.

lines.speaker: goro_grandpa
lines.jp: おう、田んぼと山、見える。
lines.en: Yeah — you can see the rice fields and mountains from it.
lines.style: Eyes crinkling with quiet pleasure. Voice opens slightly, like he's showing Sho something precious. The pace widens. A small gift of description, offered without fanfare.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.style: Unbounded energy barely contained in his small body. Voice rises bright and open. Bounces slightly in his seat. Pure, unguarded joy — the feeling bursts out before he can measure it.
